## Exploration Objectives

### Alternative Paradigm Understanding
- [ ] [Key paradigm concept 1]
- [ ] [Key paradigm concept 2] 
- [ ] [How this differs from mainstream approaches]

### Educational Goals
- [ ] Understand alternative approaches to the dominant paradigm
- [ ] Explore mathematical foundations unique to this approach
- [ ] Appreciate diversity in AI/ML methodologies
- [ ] Connect to broader themes in computational intelligence

## Exploration Checklist

### Phase 1: Paradigm Discovery (🔍)
- [ ] Research the alternative paradigm and its motivations
- [ ] Understand why this approach was developed
- [ ] Document mathematical foundations and key differences
- [ ] Identify connections to other fields (physics, biology, etc.)

### Phase 2: Focused Implementation (🔨)
- [ ] `src/config.py` - Configuration for alternative approach
- [ ] `src/data_loader.py` - Data handling (may be domain-specific)
- [ ] `src/model.py` - Core model focusing on key paradigm concepts
- [ ] `src/train.py` - Training/optimization specific to this paradigm
- [ ] `src/evaluate.py` - Evaluation appropriate for this approach
- [ ] `src/visualize.py` - Visualizations highlighting unique aspects

### Phase 3: Paradigm Comparison (💡)
- [ ] Compare with mainstream approaches from the same era
- [ ] Demonstrate unique capabilities this paradigm enables
- [ ] Show practical applications where this approach excels
- [ ] Highlight fundamental differences in problem-solving approach

### Phase 4: Broader Context (🌐)
- [ ] Connect to modern developments in this paradigm
- [ ] Discuss influence on later mainstream developments
- [ ] Explore current research directions in this area
- [ ] Identify lessons for general AI/ML understanding

## Quality Gates

### Technical Understanding
- [ ] Core paradigm concepts clearly explained
- [ ] Implementation demonstrates key principles
- [ ] Code is educational and well-documented
- [ ] Alternative approach is properly contrasted with mainstream

### Educational Value
- [ ] Broadens understanding beyond dominant paradigms
- [ ] Provides historical and conceptual context
- [ ] Encourages thinking about diverse approaches to intelligence
- [ ] Connects to broader themes in computational science

## Assessment Criteria

Students completing this side-quest should be able to:
- Explain the fundamental principles of this alternative paradigm
- Implement core concepts from scratch with clear understanding
- Compare and contrast with mainstream approaches
- Appreciate the diversity of approaches to artificial intelligence
- Understand historical context and motivation for alternative methods
